cases.input: Research a lightweight mirrorless camera for confirmed travel and sports requirements using manufacturer specifications, independent specialist reviews, user ratings and YouTube tests.
requiredBehaviors: discover a sufficiently broad candidate set and normalize exact product identities
separate manufacturer specifications from independent comparative evidence
treat user ratings as contextual signals rather than direct quality scores
classify YouTube evidence by methodology and record evidence coverage separately from quality
forbiddenBehaviors: merge different generations or variants without transferability justification
treat repeated syndicated copies as independent corroboration
convert star averages directly into product quality scores

cases.input: A newly launched product has impressive manufacturer claims and several affiliate videos, but no independent lab review and only a handful of early user reports.
requiredBehaviors: keep the product visible while assigning low or insufficient evidence coverage
mark manufacturer and affiliate evidence with appropriate independence limitations
preserve the missing independent validation as an evidence gap
forbiddenBehaviors: declare the new product quality winner from marketing volume alone
treat affiliate videos as independent validation merely because multiple channels repeat the claim

cases.input: A draft comparison mixes a 2024 base model, a 2026 Pro revision and retailer star ratings into one product record, then calls the combined average high-confidence evidence.
requiredBehaviors: reject the merged identity and require model or revision separation
separate review signals from claim evidence and lower confidence until identity is resolved
forbiddenBehaviors: accept ambiguous generations as one canonical product
use retailer stars as high-confidence comparative performance evidence
